rules.rule: General notes and specification text about hydrants are never a physical hydrant instance. A project-wide plural rule (e.g. 'ALL NEW FIRE HYDRANTS ...', 'HYDRANTS ... AS PER ... STANDARDS') or text sitting under a WATERMAIN NOTES / GENERAL NOTES / NOTES: / SPECIFICATIONS heading is logged as a general_note_or_spec mention, not counted.

negative_examples: INSTALL NEW FIRE HYDRANT FROM EXISTING 200Ø WATERMAIN

rules.rule: On a page with TYPICAL SECTION(S) / TYPICAL CROSS SECTION / TYPICAL DETAIL(S) / TYP. SECTION, a hydrant label with no site-action verb (INSTALL, SUPPLY, REPLACE, RELOCATE, REMOVE, ABANDON, DECOMMISSION, SALVAGE, TIE, CONNECT) is an illustration, never a physical instance.

rules.rule: A hydrant's station comes from a matching profile label with its printed STA (e.g. 'HYDRANT TEE AND VALVE CLUSTER' at STA 2+170.745) before the nearest chainage label. Fall back to nearest chainage only when no matching profile label exists.

negative_examples: Nearest chainage tick '2+200' near the plan callout

rules.rule: A hydrant coverage / spacing / radius annotation (COVERAGE, SPACING or RADIUS in the label or the lines stacked directly below it, with no site-action verb) describes design criteria, not a hydrant. Log it as a mention, never count it.

negative_examples: INSTALL NEW FIRE HYDRANT / MAINTAIN 1.5m SPACING FROM POLE

rules.rule: Hydrant labels can be drawn as vector outlines with no text layer. When a page has drawing content but no hydrant word in its text layer (or no text layer at all), read the page with OCR (two orientations, 150 dpi) and send the OCR lines through the same classifier and gates. Mark them provenance=ocr, confidence low. Drop OCR lines that overlap the same text already in the text layer, so nothing is counted twice.
positive_examples: HYD-05 / PROPOSED HYDRANT & VALVE (TYP) / PER MMCD W4 (outlined text on plan sheets C06-C11)
negative_examples: The same words present in the text layer at the same place
rules.negative_examples_meaning: not read again by OCR (no double count)

reader_config.note: Machine-readable patterns the Blueprint Reader app (hydrants.py v0.6+) loads at runtime. Python 're' syntax. Changing these changes reader behaviour; every run records this file's sha256 and the library commit.

not_hydrant_words.meaning: hydro ducts / hydrovac / BC Hydro are never hydrants (R-HYDRO-NOT-HYDRANT)

status_precedence.order_note: statuses are evaluated in status_wording order; tie_in first, then existing is dropped if an action status is present, then each 'beats' pair removes the loser

general_note_text.regex: ^\s*\d{1,2}\s*[.)]\s|\bMAY BE\b|\bWHERE\b|\bALL\b.*\bSHALL\b|\bSHALL NOT\b|\bWRITTEN PERMISSION\b|\bNOTIF|\bRETURN ALL\b|\bIN ACCORDANCE\b|\bLOCATIONS? TO BE CONFIRMED ON SITE\b
general_note_text.meaning: numbered notes / spec phrasing -> mention (R-LEGEND-NOT-INSTANCE / general_note_or_spec)

notes_heading.meaning: NOTES/SPECIFICATIONS heading gates the column beneath it (BR02-FP-01)

site_verb.meaning: site-action verbs that keep a label as an instance on typical/coverage gates

legend_words.regex: ^(?:WATER\s+\w+|FIRE HYDRANT(?: LEAD)?|HYDRANT(?: & VALVE ASSEMBLY)?|YARD HYDRANT|AIR VALVE|COUPLING|CAPPED END|WATER METER|WATERMAIN(?: ABD)?|SANITARY .*|STORM .*|GATE VALVE)$

profile_hydrant_label.meaning: hydrant profile label used for station pairing (BR03-02)

scope_notes.note: Existing hydrants drawn outside the work (e.g. Run 04 EX HYD-01..03) are reported as 'existing'; whether they count is not decided. The reader does not filter them.
Counts are per status and never summed.
